record.context_brief: Divergence characterization of the operator Sinkhorn algorithm
record.original_question: For operator scaling, does there exist a quantum analogue of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, or any divergence at all, such that the operator Sinkhorn algorithm can be written as an alternating minimization procedure?

evidence.quote: Since the Sinkhorn algorithm for matrix scaling is equivalent to alternating minimization of the Kullback–Leibler divergence, it is natural to ask if some quantum analogue of the Kullback–Leibler divergence yields the same characterization of the operator Sinkhorn algorithm.
However, due to the non-vanishing torsion in the space of density matrices, it is still open whether the operator Sinkhorn algorithm can be written as alternating minimization of some divergence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces of dimensions $m$ and $n$, and let $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the set of (full-rank) density matrices on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. positive-definite Hermitian operators of unit trace. A completely positive trace-preserving map (or, more generally, a completely positive map specified by Kraus operators) $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ is said to be doubly stochastic if it preserves the maximally mixed state and its adjoint does as well. The operator Sinkhorn algorithm (Gurvits' operator scaling) takes as input a completely positive map $\Phi$ and iteratively rescales it by alternately conjugating with positive-definite operators $L\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)$ and $R\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ so that $\Phi(I)$ and $\Phi^{*}(I)$ are alternately driven to the identity; i.e. it produces a sequence of scalings converging (when scalable) to a doubly stochastic map.

For ordinary (commutative) matrix scaling, the Sinkhorn iteration is well known to coincide with alternating minimization of the Kullback–Leibler divergence
$$D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)=\sum_{i,j} P_{ij}\log\frac{P_{ij}}{Q_{ij}}-P_{ij}+Q_{ij}$$
over the affine sets of nonnegative matrices with prescribed row sums and prescribed column sums, respectively.

Question. Does there exist a divergence $D(\rho\|\sigma)$ defined on pairs of (full-rank) density matrices — for instance a quantum analogue of the Kullback–Leibler divergence such as the Umegaki relative entropy, the Belavkin–Staszewski relative entropy, or any other smooth contrast function on $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H}_A)\times\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ (or on the space of completely positive maps) — such that the operator Sinkhorn algorithm coincides with alternating minimization of $D$ over two suitable affine (or e-flat) families associated with the marginal constraints $\Phi(I)=I$ and $\Phi^{*}(I)=I$?

Equivalently, given that the space of density matrices, equipped with the natural dually flat structures coming from quantum information geometry, has non-vanishing torsion, determine whether the operator Sinkhorn iteration admits a representation as alternating $D$-projections for some divergence $D$, or prove that no such divergence exists.
artifact.category_tag: Operator scaling and quantum information geometry
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on the information geometry of operator scaling shows that the operator Sinkhorn iteration can be interpreted as alternating e-projections with respect to the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) metric, but this dually flat-like structure has non-vanishing torsion, which obstructs a standard Bregman/divergence interpretation. No published result gives a divergence whose alternating minimization yields the operator Sinkhorn algorithm, and the question is described in the literature as open.

status_evidence.title: Information geometry of operator scaling
status_evidence.snippet: The operator Sinkhorn algorithm coincides with alternating e-projections with respect to the SLD metric on the space of quantum states; however the associated structure has non-vanishing torsion.
status_evidence.claim: The known information-geometric interpretation uses alternating e-projections (not divergence minimization) due to non-vanishing torsion.

status_evidence.title: Accelerating operator Sinkhorn iteration with overrelaxation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses operator Sinkhorn iteration; treats it via fixed-point/Riemannian viewpoint rather than as alternating divergence minimization.
status_evidence.claim: Current accelerations rely on Riemannian/fixed-point analyses rather than a divergence formulation, consistent with the divergence question remaining open.
